findings.failure_mode: missing or unreadable file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a domain error enum and propagate with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (non-numeric value in second field) aborts the program instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and use .map_err() on parse() to convert ParseIntError into a domain error

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 to u16 with no range check
findings.failure_mode: values greater than 65535 silently truncate, producing incorrect data instead of an error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value) and propagate the error, or validate value <= u16::MAX before casting

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses Vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-element lines cause a panic at runtime
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and handle the Some((name, rest)) / None cases explicitly

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses Vec by index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one comma-separated field panic at runtime
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and destructure the tuple (name, value_str) so both fields are guaranteed when present

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec for two-field extraction
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; the grammar is exactly two fields, making split_once sufficient
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get (name_part, value_part) without collecting into a Vec

findings.problem: println!() is an I/O side effect inside a data-processing closure
findings.failure_mode: purity is broken; the core parsing logic has observable side effects, making it untestable in isolation and coupling computation to the console
findings.fix: remove println! from the mapping closure; if logging is needed, push it to the shell layer outside the pure pipeline

findings.problem: load_orders performs fs::read_to_string (I/O) but is a public fn with no Result return type
findings.failure_mode: I/O is hidden inside a function that appears to be a pure computation; callers cannot handle file errors
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, E> from load_orders or split into a shell function (read file + log) and a pure core function (parse lines)

findings.problem: load_orders collects into Vec<Record> without any capacity reservation
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation on untrusted file size; no try_reserve or capacity hint
findings.fix: add try_reserve to the Vec with a bounded capacity computed from file metadata or a config limit, and handle AllocationError

findings.problem: Record has no validation by construction; name is a bare String, value is a bare u16
findings.failure_mode: illegal states (empty name, negative value) are representable and not rejected at construction
findings.fix: use a newtype for name (e.g. RecordName(String) with a fallible constructor that rejects empty strings) and validate value range at construction
